declared.title: A Cross-Cultural and Intra-Cultural Investigation of the Misinformation Effect in Eyewitness Memory Reports
declared.foundIn: OpenAlex search « cross-cultural differences susceptibility misinformation effect false memory culture » (2026-11-23)

population: adults in Ghana (n = 65, a collectivistic culture) and the United Kingdom (n = 62, an individualistic culture)

findings.text: On a recognition test, people from the collectivistic culture (Ghana) accepted more misleading details than people from the individualistic culture (UK)

support.sentence: However, participants from the collectivistic culture endorsed more misleading items in the recognition task than those from the individualistic culture.

findings.text: In free recall, the two cultures did not differ in how many misleading details they reported

support.sentence: Cultural differences in misinformation endorsement were not observed in free recall.

limits: two small samples (127 people), one country per culture: the authors call their findings preliminary
culture was not assigned at random: a difference between two groups, not a cause
Ghana and the UK, no Arab sample; Arab societies are often described as collectivistic, but that was not tested
